newsitem.title: DUBAI: OIC hails Iraq's acceptance of U.N. oil deal terms.
newsitem.headline: OIC hails Iraq's acceptance of U.N. oil deal terms.

text.p: The Jeddah-based Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC) on Wednesday welcomed Iraq's acceptance of U.N. terms for limited oil exports.

OIC secretary-general Hamid Algabid, in a statement telefaxed to Reuters in Dubai, described Iraq's acceptance of the oil-for-food terms as "a positive step that would contribute towards alleviating the suffering of the Iraqi people".

Iraq on Monday accepted United Nations' terms to implement a deal signed in May allowing it to sell oil worth $2 billion over six months to pay for food and medicine and some U.N. operation related to the crisis over Kuwait's seven-month occupation.
Algabid said Iraq's continued cooperation with the U.N. on implementing all Gulf War resolutions "will be a major factor in restoring peace and stability to the region".
The U.N. imposed sanctions on Iraq after it invaded Kuwait in 1990. It was driven out by a U.S.-led force in 1991.
